content.value_statement: Choosing a browser renderer without measurements can reduce accessibility and increase complexity. This skill guides renderer selection, performance diagnosis, and fallback planning.
actual_capabilities: Compare DOM, SVG, Canvas 2D, WebGL2, WebGPU, workers, WASM, and WebCodecs against product requirements.
Explain browser frame stages and identify which measurements should guide rendering changes.
Provide a Canvas 2D resizing example with capped pixel density and coordinate scaling.
Outline OffscreenCanvas transfer, worker responsibilities, feature detection, and main-thread fallback.
Assess experimental HTML-in-Canvas and CSS Paint approaches with semantic alternatives.
Guide accessibility, input coordinates, rendering budgets, device recovery, and release checks.
limitations: Provides guidance and short examples, not a complete rendering engine or benchmark suite.
Does not replace specialized documentation for routine work in an already selected GPU library.
Browser support and experimental API details require verification against current documentation.
Performance and accessibility outcomes require testing on representative browsers and devices.

use_cases.title: Select a Renderer for Interactive Charts
use_cases.description: Compare SVG and Canvas for dense charts while preserving keyboard access, labels, and equivalent data.

use_cases.title: Plan a Responsive Rendering Pipeline
use_cases.description: Evaluate whether measured main-thread rendering work justifies OffscreenCanvas, workers, and explicit compatibility fallbacks.

use_cases.title: Review Experimental Rendering Readiness
use_cases.description: Assess HTML-in-Canvas experiments for semantic alternatives, feature detection, browser coverage, and removable implementation paths.

prompt_templates.title: Choose a Starting Renderer
prompt_templates.prompt: Compare DOM, SVG, and Canvas for [interface]. Consider text selection, keyboard access, visual density, and browser targets. Recommend a starting renderer.

prompt_templates.title: Improve Canvas Resizing
prompt_templates.prompt: Review [Canvas 2D implementation] for resize behavior, pixel density, coordinate scaling, and animation scheduling. Identify missing measurements and accessibility alternatives.

prompt_templates.title: Design Worker Rendering
prompt_templates.prompt: Given [performance measurements] and [browser targets], assess OffscreenCanvas. Define worker ownership, state transfer, input handling, and a main-thread fallback.

prompt_templates.title: Review a Hybrid GPU Architecture
prompt_templates.prompt: Review [rendering architecture] combining DOM controls, WebGPU visuals, and an HTML-in-Canvas experiment. Define measurement budgets, feature gates, recovery paths, and release criteria.

output_examples.input: Which renderer should support a dense chart with searchable labels and keyboard navigation?
output: Begin with SVG when addressable elements and accessible labels meet the measured workload.
If node count becomes the measured bottleneck, evaluate Canvas for marks while keeping controls and equivalent data in DOM.
Compare frame time, interaction latency, and accessibility on target devices before changing architecture.

output_examples.input: Should we move a drawing interface to OffscreenCanvas when dragging becomes unresponsive?
output: Profile dragging to determine whether rendering, layout, or unrelated scripting blocks input.
If supported rendering work dominates, transfer canvas ownership once and keep input and semantic state on the main thread.
Send compact state updates and retain a usable main-thread renderer for unsupported browsers.

output_examples.input: Can HTML-in-Canvas become our production UI dependency?
output: Treat HTML-in-Canvas as an isolated experiment rather than a required production dependency.
Feature-detect the exact method and preserve an equivalent, visible semantic DOM path.
Review current browser support and privacy rules before testing snapshot drawing or readback.

best_practices: Measure a representative interaction and change only the layer responsible for the bottleneck.
Keep text, controls, focus behavior, and equivalent data in meaningful DOM representations.
Define browser fallbacks, pixel budgets, recovery behavior, and target-device tests before adopting specialized rendering.
anti_patterns: Choose a GPU renderer solely because it appears faster or more modern.
Replace essential text and controls with canvas pixels without equivalent semantics.
Require experimental APIs, browser flags, or origin-trial tokens for ordinary users.

faq.question: When should I use this skill?
faq.answer: Use it for renderer selection, performance architecture tradeoffs, worker rendering decisions, or experimental HTML-in-Canvas evaluation.

faq.question: Does this skill supply a rendering engine?
faq.answer: No. It supplies decision guidance, short browser examples, and review checklists.

faq.question: Is WebGPU always faster than DOM or Canvas?
faq.answer: No. The skill recommends measuring the bottleneck and choosing the least specialized renderer that meets the product need.

faq.question: Can canvas replace accessible application controls?
faq.answer: Canvas pixels do not create semantics. Keep meaningful DOM controls, keyboard behavior, focus order, and equivalent text or data.

faq.question: Should production interfaces depend on HTML-in-Canvas?
faq.answer: The skill treats it as experimental. Keep it isolated, feature-detected, and backed by a usable semantic alternative.

faq.question: What is required before using OffscreenCanvas?
faq.answer: Measure the main-thread workload, verify support in target browsers, define ownership and messaging, and retain a working fallback.
